newsitem.title: CHINA: United Tech China sales to double in 5 yrs.
newsitem.headline: United Tech China sales to double in 5 yrs.

text.p: United Technologies Corp expects annual sales in China to double over the next five years from $750 million currently, chairman George David said on Thursday.
The U.S. company also expects to expand the number of its joint ventures to about 30 by the year 2000 from 17 currently, David said.
"We will more than double sales in China over the next five years," he told reporters.
The executive said the company's sales are evenly divided among its three main businesses, Otis elevators, Carrier air conditioning equipment and Pratt & Whitney aircraft engines.
"I think we're going to see growth in all of our business areas," David said, although he added that aerospace was likely to see a somewhat stronger expansion in China in the years ahead.
The company has invested a total of $250 million in China and its joint ventures employ about 8,000 people.
David said United Technologies is discussing several projects in areas that include aerospace and automotive electrical equipment.
He declined to give details but the company has teamed up with units of the state-run Aviation Industries of China for all of its existing cooperation projects in the aerospace sector.
